assessments.summary: Decide whether a cooperative member population contains genuine segments and how many, through preprocessing ablations, null models, a gap statistic, stability analysis and a hidden-truth evaluation that includes populations with no structure.
competencies: Testing the hypothesis that clusters exist before choosing k
Designing null reference distributions and understanding how the choice of null changes the conclusion
Preprocessing heterogeneous, heavy-tailed data for distance-based methods
Cluster stability under resampling
Building a decision procedure and calibrating it on simulated ground truth
Communicating negative or ambiguous findings to a business audience

assessments.title: Whose Label Is It Anyway? Spending a Relabelling Budget on Noisy Cassava Disease Annotations
assessments.summary: Estimate label-noise rates per annotator, choose which labels to send for expert relabelling under a budget, train a noise-robust classifier, and defend the trade-offs between cleaning, discarding and modelling the noise, evaluated against hidden truth and a clean test set.
competencies: Estimating label noise without ground truth
Out-of-fold prediction for finding suspicious labels
Annotator-aware reasoning about systematic versus random error
Allocating a limited expert budget
Noise-robust training by filtering or weighting
Evaluating data-centric interventions with honest uncertainty

assessments.title: The Leaderboard That Flatters: Winner's Curse and Valid Selection in a Fraud Hackathon
assessments.summary: Quantify the winner's curse on a small public leaderboard, build a leakage-free nested validation procedure, and design and defend the evaluation protocol for the private phase of a fraud-detection hackathon.
competencies: Quantifying the winner's curse by simulation
Implementing nested cross-validation without leakage
Comparing models with paired resampling
Planning evaluation-set size from effect size and power
Shrinking noisy leaderboard scores
Designing and defending an evaluation protocol
Reporting experiments with ablations and honest uncertainty

assessments.title: When Does Depth Pay? A Controlled Study of Neural Networks Versus Boosted Trees on Small Agricultural Tables
assessments.summary: Run a controlled, seed-replicated study of when a small neural network matches or beats gradient-boosted trees and logistic regression on small synthetic soil tables, and defend a recommendation for an agricultural extension programme.
competencies: Designing a controlled comparison with factors and confounds identified
Giving each model a fair tuning budget
Replicating over seeds and reporting paired uncertainty
Locating regime boundaries (crossovers)
Separating what the data support from what the generator builds in
Writing a recommendation with stated scope
Testing study code for determinism and pairing

assessments.title: Which Roof, and Whose Village? Label-Efficient Roof Mapping with Honest Spatial Validation
assessments.summary: Classify roof material (metal, thatch, concrete tile) in synthetic aerial tiles from ten labelled villages and a pool of unlabelled tiles, quantify how much random splits overstate accuracy, compare supervised, patch-dictionary and normalised features across label budgets, and defend which claims the evidence supports.
competencies: Designing and defending a spatially blocked evaluation
Quantifying how far a random split overstates performance
Using unlabelled images through learned patch features
Isolating nuisance variation (village lighting and tint) from signal
Planning a label budget with evidence and uncertainty
Writing a validity argument for a synthetic study

assessments.title: The Scam Detector That Learned to Shout: Auditing and Hardening an SMS Filter Against Style Shortcuts
assessments.summary: Audit a synthetic SMS scam filter that relies on an urgent writing style that scammers and genuine senders later stop using consistently, find the shortcut from data with counterfactual flips, measure false-positive and recall harm across English, Pidgin and Yoruba-style messages with intervals, and defend a hardened detector and its limits.
competencies: Detecting a spurious cue from data with counterfactual tests
Choosing an operating threshold for a false-positive budget
Measuring subgroup recall and false-positive rate with intervals
Constructing a validation set that exposes a known failure mode
Comparing mitigations and defending the trade-offs
Writing a validity and harm analysis

assessments.title: After the Devaluation: Calibrated Price Forecasts Across a Structural Break
assessments.summary: Forecast a weekly staple-food price series through a synthetic currency shock: detect the break, decide how much history to trust, build calibrated 13-week prediction intervals, and argue the policy for the weeks right after a shock when almost no post-break data exists.
competencies: Detecting and dating a structural break in a short series
Choosing between full-history, rolling-window and post-break training and defending the trade-off
Building empirically calibrated multi-horizon intervals
Scoring intervals with coverage and the interval score, not width or accuracy alone
Designing controls (a no-shock series) and ablations
Arguing a policy for the period when the new regime is barely observed

assessments.title: Position Bias in the Market Feed: Learning to Rank from Clicks Without Learning Where We Put Things
assessments.summary: Learn a ranker from position-biased marketplace click logs: estimate the examination curve from a small randomised slice, build an inverse-propensity estimator for policies that were never run, train a debiased ranker, and analyse the cost and benefit of exposing small vendors.
competencies: Estimating an examination curve from a randomised slice
Computing an inverse-propensity estimate of a policy never deployed
Training a debiased ranker and comparing it with a naive click model and with the logging policy
Choosing clipping and normalisation and showing their bias-variance effect
Measuring exposure for a protected group and stating the price of changing it
Designing a monitoring plan for a feedback loop

assessments.title: Two Megabytes, Eight Languages: A Compression Study for On-Device Language Identification Under Distribution Shift
assessments.summary: Given a 2 MB hashed n-gram language-ID teacher and an unlabelled transfer pool, build size and compute accounting, a distillation routine, Pareto analysis and a selection rule, then design and defend a study of distillation, pruning, low-rank and quantisation under a clean-to-shifted message distribution gap.
competencies: Building honest size and multiply-add cost models
Distilling a teacher onto a smaller student using unlabelled data
Constructing and reading Pareto frontiers across several objectives
Evaluating models under distribution shift rather than on clean data
Selecting a deployable model with a small validation set and stating the uncertainty
Writing a study protocol with hypotheses, controls and threats to validity

assessments.title: The Month Before the Labels Arrive: Designing a Safe Rollout for a Replacement Credit Model
assessments.summary: Using a deterministic rollout simulator with delayed loan outcomes, hidden segment-level harm and silent failures, implement the statistics and an auditable rollout controller that rolls back harmful replacement models quickly, promotes good ones in reasonable time, and defend the stage, guardrail and threshold design with ablations.
competencies: Designing a staged rollout with explicit entry and exit criteria
Combining immediate proxy guardrails with lagged outcome evidence
Protecting a small segment from harm hidden by the overall average
Testing non-inferiority with a stated margin
Quantifying the harm-versus-delay trade-off with a simulator
Writing an automated controller whose every decision is explained

assessments.title: When to Retrain the Harvest-Loan Model: Cost, Label Delay and Drift Regimes in a Retraining-Policy Study
assessments.summary: Build a delayed-label retraining simulator, design competing retraining policies, and defend a recommendation across abrupt, gradual and seasonal drift under explicit retraining and error costs, including how the answer changes with the cost and the label delay.
competencies: Building a simulator that enforces label delay and cost accounting
Designing retraining triggers and training-window rules
Choosing among policies under uncertainty about the drift regime
Quantifying how a recommendation depends on cost and delay assumptions
Arguing the validity and limits of a synthetic policy study

assessments.title: Do the Explanations Tell the Truth? Faithfulness, Stability and Shortcut Audits for a Tuberculosis-Screening Model
assessments.summary: Build permutation importance, sampled Shapley values, deletion-based faithfulness, stability and agreement measures and a deployment-shift shortcut audit, then study whether explanations expose a planted device shortcut across model classes, backgrounds and correlated features, and what they cannot prove.
competencies: Implementing attribution methods whose properties can be tested exactly
Measuring explanation faithfulness, stability and agreement
Auditing for shortcuts using a deployment-like sample
Reasoning about baselines, correlated features and what attribution cannot show
Writing a validity-aware interpretability study for a clinical audience
